findings.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Attacker-controlled bytes with an image extension are fed to `convert` BEFORE any content validation (FastImage/Upload.create_for), so a `.png` that is really MVG/PS/SVG/PDF drives ImageMagick delegates (Ghostscript, librsvg, ImageTragick-class coders) from a plain logged-in upload; previously IM only ran on files that had already passed magic-byte validation.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Up to 5 `convert` + `ImageOptim` passes on a 10MB pixel flood run with no `-limit memory/map/area`, no timeout, inside the web process (Scheduler::Defer thread, not covered by unicorn's request timeout, and single-queued so every other deferred task in that worker stalls); any logged-in user can repeat this as a cheap CPU/RAM DoS.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored: `convert` writes in place (same inode, `fopen "wb"`), so if it dies mid-write (OOM kill, disk full) the tempfile is truncated, the loop exits because the size is now small, and the corrupt file is handed to `Upload.create_for` (FastImage only reads the header, so it can pass) and persisted with no original left to fall back on.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — tempfile.size` is fstat on the Rack tempfile's open fd, but `convert_with` runs `ImageOptim.optimize_image!` which replaces the path via rename (new inode); after pass 1 the fd points at the orphaned pre-optim inode, so the loop condition never sees later shrinkage, passes 2-5 are wasted, and `Upload.create_for(tempfile, ..., tempfile.size)` stores stale bytes/size (store copies via `file.read`) while `Digest::SHA1.file` hashes the path's new inode, giving a sha1 that does not match the stored content.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:129 — Large animated GIFs are silently destroyed: with `allow_animated_thumbnails` (default false) the non-animated path uses `#{from}[0]`, rewriting the user's original in place as a single-frame image; with it enabled, gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%` rejects a percentage (expects WxH) so every pass fails and the file stays oversized.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — FileHelper.is_image?` includes `.svg`, so oversized SVGs are run through `convert in.svg -resize 80% in.svg` which rasterizes the vector and rewrites the .svg in place (and exposes the XML/SVG delegate to XXE/SSRF and huge-viewbox memory bombs); `OptimizedImage.create_for` deliberately special-cases svg with a plain copy, this loop does not.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:68 — The loop has no success check: after 5 failed or ineffective passes (non-shrinkable metadata-padded image, missing `convert` binary, non-image bytes) it proceeds to `Upload.create_for` regardless; correctness now depends entirely on the downstream UploadValidator size check, which is neither in this diff nor guarded here, and each failure still costs 5 process spawns.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — self.downsize` is defined twice; the 3-arg version at :149 silently replaces the 5-arg version at :145, so any caller passing `(from, to, w, h, opts)` now gets `w` as the geometry and the Integer `h` as `opts`, raising TypeError at `opts[:allow_animation]` (:155); the :145 definition is dead code and a `ruby -w` "method redefined" warning.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client size check is hardcoded to 10MB for ALL upload types, replacing `max_<type>_size_kb`: attachments are no longer checked against `max_attachment_size_kb` (an admin's stricter limit is bypassed client-side, forcing a full 10MB upload before the server rejects), while a looser admin limit (>10MB) is now impossible, and the "file_too_large" alert reports 10240KB which contradicts the server's real limit in the follow-up error.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL download cap raised from `max_image_size_kb` to a flat 10MB for every `type`, including attachments, ignoring `max_attachment_size_kb` and letting an API caller make the server pull 10MB from an arbitrary URL per request (the loop in `FileHelper.download` also overshoots the cap by a chunk).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Every pass re-encodes JPEGs (no `-quality`, followed by ImageOptim) so up to 5 lossy generations degrade the persisted original; the required scale factor could be computed once from `sqrt(max/size)` instead of iterating.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler now claims a fixed 10MB limit regardless of the actual nginx `client_max_body_size`, giving misleading guidance when an admin has changed it.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently discards the 5-arity `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined at line 145 (Ruby "method redefined" warning), so any existing caller passing width, height, opts (e.g. Upload.create_for profile/card background downsizing) now raises ArgumentError "given 5, expected 3..4".

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — tempfile.size` is fstat on the still-open Rack tempfile fd, but `convert_with` runs `ImageOptim#optimize_image!` which replaces `tempfile.path` via rename (new inode); after the first successful pass the fd is stale so the loop condition never sees further shrinkage (runs all 5 passes, over-shrinking to ~33% width) and the `filesize` passed to `Upload.create_for` on line 72 is the pre-optimization size.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — For `.gif` uploads with `allow_animated_thumbnails` on, `optimize` routes to `downsize_instructions_animated` which passes "80%" to gifsicle `--resize-fit`, which only accepts WIDTHxHEIGHT; every attempt fails so oversized GIFs are never downsized and are then rejected by Upload.create_for after 5 wasted subprocess spawns.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored, so when `convert`/gifsicle fails the loop re-runs the identical failing command up to 5 times and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with whatever (possibly partially written) file `convert` left at `tempfile.path`.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — In-place `from == to` downsize uses `downsize_instructions` with `#{from}[0]`, so a multi-frame image that takes the non-animated path (any GIF when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is off, multi-page TIFF) has all frames but the first silently discarded from the stored original.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Guard is `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, which in Discourse includes `svg` (see the svg special-case at optimized_image.rb:45), so an oversized SVG is run through `convert big.svg[0] -resize 80% big.svg` and rasterized/rewritten by ImageMagick instead of being kept as vector or rejected.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — validateUploadedFile` is shared by `type` "image" and "attachment"; hardcoding 10MB drops the client-side `max_attachment_size_kb` check, so attachments larger than the admin limit but under 10MB are uploaded only to be rejected server-side, and attachments over 10MB are blocked even when the admin allows them.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit, but a 413 comes from the web server body-size limit which is not tied to this constant, so the message can state the wrong maximum.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Up to 5 sequential full-file ImageMagick convert passes (plus ImageOptim each) on inputs up to 10MB run inside the web worker (synchronously for API, or in the in-process Scheduler::Defer thread) instead of a Sidekiq job like the adjacent create_thumbnails at line 80.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:132 — downsize_instructions spawns convert with no -limit memory/map/area/time and no cheap dimension precheck, so a 10MB (now allowed) high-megapixel or decompression-bomb PNG/JPEG can consume GBs of RAM/CPU per pass in the web process.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:164 — Each loop pass runs ImageOptim.new.optimize_image! (new resolver + lossless optimizers like optipng/pngcrush/jpegtran) whose output is immediately re-decoded and re-encoded by the next convert, so up to 4 of 5 expensive optimizer runs are thrown away.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored, so on failure (convert error, or gifsicle rejecting the "80%" geometry for GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is on) the identical command is re-run 4 more times for nothing.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — Fixed 80% linear per pass yields only ~11% pixel area after 5 passes (0.8^10), so a 10MB file can never get under a max_image_size_kb of ~1MB or less yet all 5 passes are still paid before the oversized file goes to Upload.create_for; computing one scale from sqrt(limit/size) would do it in a single convert.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side check now ignores type and hardcodes 10MB, so attachments/avatars above their configured max_*_size_kb are fully uploaded (bandwidth + tempfile + server work) before the server can reject them.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL path now downloads up to 10MB regardless of type or max_image_size_kb, so non-image or already-too-large fetches do 10MB of network/disk work before validation.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (false on convert/ImageOptim failure) is ignored, so a failed or partially-written in-place conversion (from == to, same inode truncated by convert) silently passes the size check and falls through to Upload.create_for, creating an Upload from a corrupted/truncated file (FastImage rescue nil yields 0x0 dims).

app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — &> /dev/null` is a bashism; Ruby backticks use /bin/sh, and under dash (Debian/Ubuntu, the Discourse docker base) it parses as `convert ... &` + `> /dev/null`, so convert runs in the background, `$?` is 0 immediately, and ImageOptim, the loop's tempfile.size check and Upload.create_for all race against a still-writing in-place convert (verified locally with dash).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Tempfile#size fstats the open fd, but ImageOptim#optimize_image! (image_optim 0.20.2 ImagePath#replace) renames a new inode over the path each pass, so `tempfile.size` returns the stale pre-optimisation size both for the loop condition and for the `filesize` handed to Upload.create_for/UploadValidator (can reject an image that is actually under max_image_size_kb on disk and records a wrong filesize).

app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — No timeout or ImageMagick resource limits (`-limit memory/time`) on the external convert/gifsicle/image_optim processes, which now run synchronously in the web process (request thread or Scheduler::Defer thread) on untrusted files up to 10MB, up to 5 passes each followed by ImageOptim; a decompression-bomb image can pin a unicorn worker's CPU/RAM indefinitely.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:72 — After a downsize pass the Tempfile handle points at the old unlinked inode, while Upload.create_for computes sha1 via the path (new inode) and LocalStore#copy_file writes `file.read` from the handle (old inode), so stored bytes, sha1 and filesize can disagree for every auto-downsized image (pre-existing for the ImageOptim call inside create_for, now triggered on the request path for all large images).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With allow_animated_thumbnails false (the default), downsize_instructions uses `#{from}[0]` and writes in place, so an oversized animated GIF is permanently flattened to its first frame before the original is stored, destroying user data rather than merely producing a static thumbnail.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:137 — The animated path passes the "80%" dimension string to gifsicle `--resize-fit`, which only accepts WxH (percent scaling is `--scale`), so gifsicle exits non-zero every pass; the loop burns all 5 attempts and animated GIFs are never downsized, falling through to a validator rejection.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` silently overrides the 5-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined four lines earlier (Ruby has no overloading); the first definition is dead and any caller using the old arity now raises ArgumentError or passes height as `opts` (TypeError on `opts[:allow_animation]`).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — FileHelper.is_image? matches .svg, so an oversized SVG is run through `convert file.svg[0] ... file.svg` in place (rasterised or failed output); Upload.create_for then Nokogiri-parses it and `at_css("svg")` may be nil, raising inside the Scheduler::Defer block (no rescue in create_upload) so the client never receives the MessageBus result.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — rescue nil` swallows all FileHelper.download errors and leaves `tempfile` nil; the new guard on line 64 handles nil but line 72 still calls `tempfile.size`, raising NoMethodError with no error reported to the API caller (pre-existing, unchanged by the PR).

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side pre-flight cap is hardcoded to 10MB for every upload type (attachments included) while the server still validates attachments against max_attachment_size_kb and images against max_image_size_kb (which may exceed 10MB), so the client check diverges from server behaviour and the 413 message reports 10MB regardless of the real nginx/site limit.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Untrusted images (now up to 10MB) are looped up to 5x through ImageMagick convert with no memory/pixel/time limits, enabling decompression-bomb / CPU-memory DoS

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:181 — Client size cap hardcoded to 10MB ignores admin max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb, and oversized files are still passed to Upload.create_for when 5 downsize passes fail to shrink below the limit

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — New 5-pass/80% auto-downsize loop ships with zero test coverage (the snapshot has no spec/ or test/ dirs and the diff adds none); nothing exercises an upload larger than max_image_size_kb end to end.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Upstream test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6 "prevents files that are too big from being uploaded" sets max_image_size_kb=5 and expects a 10KB image to be rejected; the hardcoded 10MB cap makes that assertion fail (file absent from this snapshot, verify in full checkout).

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler now alerts "10240 KB" regardless of the site setting and no JS test covers displayErrorForUpload's 413 branch, so the wrong number in the user-facing message goes unnoticed.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — Downsize failure path is untested: when `convert`/ImageOptim fails, convert_with returns false, the loop silently burns all 5 attempts and falls through to Upload.create_for with the still-oversized file; no spec asserts the resulting too_large error or that a partially written tempfile is not persisted.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Animated GIF edge case has no coverage: Rack multipart tempfile paths carry no extension so `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` never matches and `convert #{from}[0]` keeps only the first frame, while API-downloaded tempfiles do keep the extension and go through gifsicle; a spec uploading an oversized animated GIF via both paths would expose the inconsistency.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — No test asserts `tempfile.size` (fstat on the already-open fd) reflects the file rewritten in place by an external `convert` process, so both the loop's termination condition and the `filesize` passed to Upload.create_for could be stale without any test catching it.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — Guard conditions are untested: max_image_size_kb = 0 must disable downsizing, non-image attachments must be skipped, SVG (matched by FileHelper.is_image?) must not be rasterised/corrupted by `convert -resize 80%` into an extensionless output, and an empty tempfile must be skipped.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL download limit changed from max_image_size_kb to 10.megabytes with no spec; upstream uploads_controller_spec stubs FileHelper.download/Upload.create_for so it neither breaks nor verifies the new limit or that URL-downloaded images also get downsized.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:146 — Duplicate `def self.downsize` silently replaces the 5-arg (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) version; no spec exercises downsize at all, so any remaining 5-arity caller would only fail at runtime (max_height swallowed as opts) with nothing to catch it.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:141 — Upstream spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb stubs `OptimizedImage.resize` wholesale, so the resize/optimize signature change and removal of `OptimizedImage.dimensions` are not verified by any test; an instruction-level spec should assert resize forwards "WxH" and downsize forwards "80%" to `*_instructions`.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — A spec that merely mocks `OptimizedImage.downsize` would only verify the call count; the feature needs an integration test with a real >max_image_size_kb fixture asserting the persisted Upload's filesize is <= the limit, width/height shrank, and at most 5 passes ran.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:70 — Untested semantic change: the tempfile is mutated before Upload.create_for computes sha1/width/height, so sha1 dedupe now depends on max_image_size_kb and ImageMagick output rather than the original bytes; no spec pins this behaviour.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a pre-processing loop in `create_upload` that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, ...)` (which ultimately shells out to ImageMagick via `convert_with`) before `Upload.create_for(...)` is invoked. The only gating shown is `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, which is based on the `filename` value (extension-derived in the URL case) rather than any shown magic-byte/content validation. Therefore attacker-controlled bytes can reach ImageMagick before the later upload creation/validation step, matching the reported risk.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a while-loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that can run up to 5 times per upload, repeatedly calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` until the tempfile is under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (new block at lines ~66-73). `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes the ImageMagick command via backticks with no timeout or resource limits (`\`#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null\``), so a maliciously expensive image can force multiple potentially long-running `convert` invocations in the request path. The finding’s extra details about `Scheduler::Defer`/unicorn timeouts aren’t shown in the diff, but the core DoS risk from unbounded external image processing loops is directly introduced here.

adjudication.rationale: The new upload logic downsizes images in-place (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`) inside a loop but never checks whether the downsize/convert succeeded; it only re-checks `tempfile.size`. If the conversion fails (and `convert_with` can return `false` on non-zero exit), the code still proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` with whatever is in the tempfile, potentially a partially-written/corrupt file or a file still exceeding `max_image_size_kb` after 5 attempts. This lack of error handling is introduced by the diff and is a real correctness/data-integrity risk.

This becomes a real correctness issue in this PR because new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` in a loop and immediately checks `tempfile.size`, so returning before the conversion finishes can cause races/incorrect size checks and uploads against a still-being-written file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Animated GIF edge case has no coverage: Rack multipart tempfile paths carry no extension so `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` never matches and `convert #{from}[0]` keeps only the first frame, while API-downloaded tempfiles do keep the extension and go through gifsicle; a spec uploading an oversized animated GIF via both paths would expose the inconsistency.
